group.passage:
Food waste is a pressing issue. According to the UNEP Food Waste Index 2024, approximately 1.05 billion tons of food waste was generated in 2022, which means 19% of food available to consumers was wasted. [[1]] Now, an innovative app called “Too Good To Go” may be the ideal way to make that happen.
Founded in Copenhagen in 2015 by young entrepreneurs who shared a dream of seeking a solution to the massive amount of food waste, Too Good To Go connects users with restaurants and supermarkets that have excess food. The concept behind it is simple yet effective. Each day, participating stores offer “magic bags” on the app, which contain a selection of unsold food. [[2]] Customers typically don’t know what food is inside the bags until they pick them up, adding an element of surprise. This approach not only ensures that users get an assortment of food but also helps businesses clear their shelves of unsold food items. [[3]] These are food items that might otherwise have ended up in a landfill. As a result, the app has caught on with students and workers looking to reduce their food costs.
[[4]] By promoting a zero-waste approach to food consumption, the app further fosters a community where users value frugality and environmental responsibility. With its growing popularity, Too Good To Go is encouraging a shift towards a more sustainable future.

options_bank.A: After app users log in, they can browse the platform, select their favorite store, and then place an order.
options_bank.B: The impact of Too Good To Go goes beyond individual savings and business benefits.
options_bank.C: If properly utilized, the surpluses could benefit 2.4 billion people who lack access to sufficient food.
options_bank.D: Sometimes users strike gold with an incredible value, such as $3 for ten bagels and two salads.

tags.topic: the Too Good To Go app reducing food waste
